info.title: FluxDB API
info.description:
FluxDB exposes three HTTP surfaces against one storage engine.

`/api/v1` is the single-tenant administration API, authenticated by one shared bearer token (`bearerAuth`). It names engine databases directly and so sits underneath project isolation; it is what a self-hosted server, the SDKs and the offline CLI use.

`/api/ingest/v1` is for agents and applications on a hosted deployment, authenticated by a project API key (`apiKeyAuth`) with read and write scopes. A key reaches only its own project's buckets.

`/api/cloud` is the console's API, authenticated by the session cookie (`sessionCookie`). Data is addressed as project plus bucket; a caller can never name an engine database.

Timestamps are decimal nanosecond strings and exact 64-bit integers are `{"integer": "…"}`, because an IEEE-754 double cannot represent the whole i64 range. Query results return both as strings for the same reason.

post.summary: Write points in InfluxDB line protocol
post.description: The format most metrics agents already emit. Integers carry an `i` suffix; commas, spaces and equals signs inside keys and tag values are backslash-escaped. A line with no timestamp is stamped on arrival.

parameters.description: Target bucket name. Optional when the project has exactly one bucket. `db` is accepted as an alias so InfluxDB-shaped agent configuration works unchanged.

bearerAuth.description: The shared FLUXDB_TOKEN. Grants server-wide administration over /api/v1.

apiKeyAuth.description: A project API key, `fdbk_{id}_{secret}`, created in the console. Scoped to one project and to read and/or write.

sessionCookie.name: flux_session
sessionCookie.description: HttpOnly session cookie issued by the sign-in endpoints. Only its SHA-256 is stored server-side.

timestamp.description: Signed i64 Unix nanoseconds; never a JSON number

code.description: Stable machine-readable reason on control-plane responses: invalid_request, unauthenticated, forbidden, not_found, conflict, quota_exceeded, rate_limited, internal.

rows.description: Timestamps and 64-bit integers are decimal strings.

window.description: The resolved range the macros expanded to.

query.description: One SELECT from the documented subset. May contain $timeFilter, $interval, $from and $to.

from.description: Inclusive start, decimal nanoseconds. Defaults to six hours ago.

to.description: Inclusive end, decimal nanoseconds. Defaults to now.

interval.description: Bucket width for $interval. Chosen automatically when omitted.
